s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of a generalized eruption with fever and systemic involvement in a patient with a history of autoimmune disease
salient_findings: Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face
Several large bullae on the right arm
Numerous flat and raised atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Worsening, exquisitely tender rash with several blisters across right arm
key_facts: Patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus
Patient was hospitalized 6 days prior for a photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus
Temperature of 101.5°F
Normocytic anemia with mean corpuscular volume of 99 fL, hemoglobin of 11.7 g/dL, and hematocrit of 33.4%
Thrombocytopenia with platelet count of 81 K/μL
Hypocomplementemia with C3 of 42 mg/dL and C4 of 3 mg/dL
Antinuclear antibody titer of 1:1280 with speckled pattern
Positive anti-Smith, antiribonucleoprotein, and SSA/anti-Ro antibodies
Negative bacterial blood, urine, stool, and cerebrospinal fluid cultures
Negative hepatitis panel
Punch biopsy of abdominal target lesion showed dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a generalized eruption with fever, bullae, and target lesions, which are characteristic of Stevens-Johnson Syndrome

shortlist.label: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a severe skin reaction with widespread bullae and erosions, which is consistent with Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis

shortlist.label: Acute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus and is experiencing a photo-induced flare, which is consistent with Acute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus

shortlist.label: Bullous Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus and is experiencing bullae, which is consistent with Bullous Lupus Erythematosus

shortlist.label: Erythema Multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a generalized eruption with target lesions, which is consistent with Erythema Multiforme

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fever, generalized eruption, and target lesions, along with the presence of bullae and mucosal involvement, is most consistent with Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, a severe cutaneous adverse reaction. The patient's recent hospitalization for a photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus and the presence of autoantibodies may have predisposed her to this condition.

rejected.label: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
rejected.why: While similar to Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis typically involves more widespread skin detachment and a higher mortality rate, which is not explicitly mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Acute Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of systemic lupus erythematosus and was recently hospitalized for a photo-induced flare of acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, the current presentation of target lesions and bullae is more suggestive of Stevens-Johnson Syndrome.

rejected.label: Bullous Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: Bullous Lupus Erythematosus is a rare manifestation of lupus erythematosus characterized by bullae, but the patient's presentation of target lesions and fever is more consistent with Stevens-Johnson Syndrome.

rejected.label: Erythema Multiforme
rejected.why: Erythema Multiforme is a skin condition characterized by target lesions, but it typically does not involve the severity of symptoms, such as fever and bullae, seen in this patient.
